newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sources say govt picks telecoms regulator.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sources say govt picks telecoms regulator.

text.p: German government sources said on Tuesday that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition had agreed to appoint Dieter Scheuerle, a senior postal ministry official, to head the new telecoms Regulatory Agency.

Although widely expected, the choice has been controversial because of criticism from the telecommunications industry which fears Scheuerle will be tough in regulating Deutsche Telekom, the incumbent monopoly, as the market is opened to competition.
The Regulatory Council, a temporary body made up of representatives of state governments and parliament, had proposed appointing Peter Landsberg, former chairman of Alcatel SEL.
The new watchdog, the Regulatory Agency, will be under the wing of the economics ministry and begins operating on January 1, 1998, when the telecoms sector is opened to full competition.

According to government sources, Scheuerle will head the new agency and he will have two deputies -- Arne Boernsen, the Social Democratic (SPD) chairman of parliament's postal affairs committee, and Volker Schlegel, head of the economics department at the German Embassy in Washington.
Germany's Federation of Taxpayers called the decision a classic example of cronyism and sharply criticised the size of the salaries the three officials would receive.
The Federal Accounting Office has also criticised the salaries, which are higher than at any other state agency.
As head of the agency, Scheuerle will receive a monthly salary of 18,535 marks ($10,600), while his deputies will each receive 14,573 marks.
